Q1.name: Achieves its purpose
Q1.test: MET when the page does what a page of its type is for — informs, sells, explains who someone is, lets the reader act — and a reader arriving for that purpose would be satisfied. UNMET when the purpose is unclear, unfulfilled, or buried. Judge the purpose first (QRG §2.2), then whether the main content achieves it.

Q2.name: Target keyword in the title, once
Q2.test: The declared primary keyword, or a close variant, appears in the <title>; the same phrase is not repeated.

Q3.name: Serves the keyword's intent
Q3.test: MET when the page answers the declared query's dominant intent (Know, Know Simple, Do, Website or Visit-in-person, QRG §12.7) and its most likely interpretation. UNMET when a searcher with that query would need another page.

Q4.name: Covers the query's real sub-questions in one page
Q4.test: MET when the page answers the searchers' real follow-up questions about its own subject (from People-also-ask / related searches) within this page. On a page with a SITE ROLE as a spoke of a hub, questions about the topic in general may be left to that hub when the page links to it — answering them here would compete with the hub. UNMET when obvious follow-up questions about the page's own subject go unanswered, or are pushed to thin separate pages.

Q5.name: No keyword stuffing
Q5.test: No unnatural, out-of-context repetition of the target term or its variants.

Q6.name: Title and H1 match the content
Q6.test: MET when the page title and H1 accurately describe the main content. UNMET when either exaggerates, shocks, or promises something the page does not deliver (QRG §5.2 Low-title examples).

Q7.name: Page-specific meta description
Q7.test: MET when a meta description is present and summarises this particular page. UNMET when it is missing, generic boilerplate shared across pages, or describes something else. Length alone is not a failure.

C1.name: Effort and originality
C1.test: MET when the main content adds something beyond what is commonly available: first-hand experience, original analysis, synthesis, or evident expertise and effort (QRG §3.2). UNMET when it restates commodity information anyone could assemble.

C2.name: Facts correct and consistent with expert consensus
C2.test: MET when statements of fact are accurate and consistent with well-established expert consensus. UNMET when any is clearly inaccurate, or contradicts consensus without saying so (QRG §4.4; fiction, satire, clearly marked opinion and reasonably debatable claims are excluded). A true finding stated too strongly is judged under C9, not here; a falsehood that could harm a reader is judged under C12.

C3.name: Complete for its purpose
C3.test: MET when the page carries the facts its type and purpose need: price, specifications and availability on a product; method, sample and limits on an evidence page; the steps on an instructional page; the key facts on an article. UNMET when a reader must go elsewhere for an essential fact.

C4.name: Internally consistent
C4.test: MET when figures, claims, names and dates agree throughout the page. UNMET when the page contradicts itself.

C5.name: Specific, sourced evidence
C5.test: MET when specific numbers, definitions and comparisons are attributed to a source a reader can check (named study, linked source, reference list). UNMET when specific claims are made without any traceable source.

C6.name: Main content prominent and unobstructed
C6.test: No filler before the main content; no ad, overlay or intrusive interstitial covering it.

C7.name: Clear structure
C7.test: MET when headings and sections let a reader find their way through the content. UNMET when a long page is an undivided wall or headings do not describe their sections. Do not count headings or paragraph lengths.

C8.name: Not copied, not machine boilerplate
C8.test: No verbatim copying from the open web; no LLM boilerplate strings.

C9.name: Claims proportionate to the evidence
C9.test: MET when claims stay within their sources: study results are not presented as proof for a product the study did not test, recommendation strength matches evidence strength, and there is no hype. UNMET when any claim outruns the evidence given for it.

C10.name: Produced with care
C10.test: MET when spelling, grammar and names (brand, ingredient, product, person) are correct and consistent, and no block or paragraph is duplicated. UNMET when there are repeated errors, inconsistent names, or duplicated passages.

C11.name: Comparisons and reviews show their evidence and method
C11.test: Applies only where the page reviews, compares or ranks products or options; otherwise answer NA. MET when it says why, with first-hand evidence, benefits and drawbacks, and how items were compared. UNMET when rankings or verdicts are asserted without method or evidence.

C12.name: No harmfully misleading information
C12.test: MET when nothing on the page is false or misleading in a way that could harm a reader who acted on it. UNMET when a clearly inaccurate statement, a contradiction of expert consensus, or an unsubstantiated theory could lead a reader to harm their health, money or safety — for example an unsafe dose, frequency or combination, a claim to cure or treat a disease, or advice to avoid professional care (QRG §4.4; trivial errors, fiction, satire, clearly marked opinion and reasonably debatable claims are excluded).

R1.name: Responsible entity identified
R1.test: MET when it is clear who is responsible for the page (organisation or person), and a reader can find how to contact them. UNMET when responsibility is hidden or unclear (QRG §2.5.2-2.5.3).

R2.name: Byline where a reader expects one
R2.test: MET when the page says, with its content or in the article header above it, who wrote or compiled it — a named person, or a named team or organisation ("By the Skingenetix research team" counts). UNMET when an article, evidence page or profile carries no author a reader can see at all. Whether the named author is credible is judged elsewhere, not here.
R2.source: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content (Who); Google author markup accepts Person or Organization

R3.name: Credentials truthful
R3.test: MET when stated author or reviewer credentials are specific, plausible and consistent with what the page shows, and no review is claimed without a named reviewer. UNMET when credentials are vague, overstated, or implausible. Absent credentials are not UNMET — only false or overstated ones.

R4.name: Citations resolve to what they claim
R4.test: Every DOI/PMID/URL cited resolves, and to the work named beside it.

R5.name: Commercial interest disclosed
R5.test: MET when any material commercial relationship — the publisher selling what it recommends, affiliate links, sponsorship — is disclosed where it bears on the claims, and promotion is distinguishable from information. UNMET when it is hidden.

R6.name: Customer service reachable
R6.test: MET when contact, returns, shipping and payment help are reachable from the page. UNMET when a buyer cannot find them.

R7.name: Visible, accurate date
R7.test: MET when a published or last-updated (or last-reviewed) date is visible with the content or in the article header above it, and plausible. UNMET when no date is visible where readers need one.

R8.name: Reviews genuine and shown
R8.test: Applies only where the page shows or marks up reviews or ratings; otherwise answer NA. MET when review content is visible and plausibly from customers. UNMET when ratings appear without visible reviews.

R9.name: Independent reputation
R9.test: What independent sources say about the site and creator.

S1.name: Markup matches visible content
S1.test: Marked-up name/headline/price/rating appear on the page.

S2.name: Valid for types that have rules
S2.test: Required properties and value types on types that still have them.

S3.name: The type that fits the page
S3.test: Product on product, Article family on article/evidence, Organization on home/about, ProfilePage on profile.

S4.name: Time-sensitive markup current
S4.test: No past Event.endDate, expired JobPosting or stale Offer.priceValidUntil.

S5.name: Markup survives rendering
S5.test: JSON-LD present in raw and rendered DOM.

A1.name: Snippet-eligible for AI features
A1.test: No nosnippet / max-snippet:0 in robots meta or X-Robots-Tag; no data-nosnippet over main content.

A2.name: AI search crawlers allowed
A2.test: robots.txt allows OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot and Claude-SearchBot.

A3.name: Main content in the server HTML
A3.test: The substantive main content is present without JavaScript.
A3.source: Vercel first-party crawler logs (GPTBot/ClaudeBot do not execute JS)

A4.name: Key facts stated in self-contained sentences
A4.test: MET when the page's key answer and definitions can be understood and quoted without the surrounding paragraphs. UNMET when essential facts only make sense in context ("as mentioned above", pronouns without referents). This is judged for readers; it is not a citation lever.

P1.name: Keyword owned by one page
P1.test: No other page in the site keyword map has this page's primary keyword.

P2.name: No second own URL competing
P2.test: At most one own URL ranks for the declared keyword.

P3.name: Linked into its cluster
P3.test: Links up to its hub and across to a sibling; the hub links back.

P4.name: Descriptive internal anchors
P4.test: MET when the page's links to other pages on the site use anchor text that tells the reader what the target is. UNMET when anchors are generic ("click here", "read more", bare URLs).

P5.name: Distinct from its siblings
P5.test: Main content not a near-duplicate of declared siblings.

O1.name: Earned links to this URL
O1.test: Referring domains to the URL against SERP competitors.

O2.name: Natural anchor profile
O2.test: Exact-match share of backlink anchors not excessive (a risk flag).

T1.name: Core Web Vitals (field)
T1.test: LCP ≤ 2.5 s, INP ≤ 200 ms, CLS ≤ 0.1 at p75 from field data.

T3.name: Works on a phone
T3.test: Viewport; no horizontal scroll at 390 px; tap targets.

T4.name: Reachable in the site graph
T4.test: Linked from the site; in the sitemap.

T6.name: Descriptive image alt text
T6.test: MET when content images carry alt text that describes them. UNMET when content images lack alt text or use filenames or keywords instead of descriptions. Answer NA when the page has no content images.

T7.name: No broken links or resources
T7.test: No broken internal links or missing images.

X1.name: One clear primary action, with proof beside it
X1.test: MET when the page offers one clear next action for a visitor who is ready, with supporting evidence next to the ask. On an evidence or article page a next step is optional: MET when any call to action comes after the evidence and does not compete with it. UNMET when there is no clear action where one is expected, or several compete.

X2.name: Objections and next steps answered
X2.test: MET when the page tells the visitor what happens next, what it costs, how long it takes and who they deal with. UNMET when those obvious questions go unanswered.

X3.name: Accessible basics
X3.test: Contrast AA, focus, tap targets, 200% zoom. Not a ranking factor.
X3.source: Rule 27 Check A; European Accessibility Act

V1.name: Safety information present
V1.test: Applies to health, cosmetic and supplement topics; otherwise answer NA. MET when side effects, contraindications, interactions and when to see a professional are given where relevant. UNMET when a reader could act on the page without knowing a relevant risk.
V1.source: https://static.googleusercontent.com/media/guidelines.raterhub.com/en//searchqualityevaluatorguidelines.pdf §3.4 ("Trust: Consider the extent to which the page is accurate, honest, safe, and reliable") — an interpretation, not an explicit QRG requirement; premium-brand practice (Medik8, INKEY, Timeless, Murad). Research 2026-09-30: skingenetix-website docs/research-2026-09-30-safety-notes-on-study-articles.md

V2.name: No medicinal claim on a cosmetic product
V2.test: Applies to cosmetic products and their claims; otherwise answer NA. MET when every claim stays within cosmetic function (appearance, feel, cleansing, protection). UNMET when the page claims to treat, cure, prevent or heal a condition.
V2.source: EU Regulation 655/2013 — article citation to verify before scoring

V3.name: Study design disclosed on evidence pages
V3.test: MET when an evidence page states the study's sample, population, design, funding and limitations. UNMET when any of these is missing.

V4.name: No outcome promises
V4.test: Applies to health, cosmetic and supplement topics; otherwise answer NA. MET when results are stated with their evidence and variability. UNMET when the page guarantees or implies certain results.

V5.name: Regulatory status stated and true
V5.test: Applies where a product has a regulatory status (cosmetic, CE-marked device, food supplement, medicine); otherwise answer NA. MET when that status is stated and consistent with how the product is described. UNMET when it is missing or contradicted.
V5.source: regulatory sources to cite before scoring
